replies.author: @lukask7445
replies.text:
At least every second town is worth visiting and some of the second- or third-tier ones boast more valuable historical landmarks than many of the top destinations.
While these smaller towns suffer from dismal transport connectivity and occasional isolation from the rail network, the clear winners are the major cities. They feature local airports served by low-cost carriers and situated remarkably close to their centers, offering exceptionally economical public transit from about $1.50. Additionally, traveling between these large urban hubs via train is highly cost-effective, thanks to wallet-friendly rail fares.
A serious and strongly motivated tourist can rent a car. Poland has been developing an excellent motorway network that—despite the country's considerable size (being roughly square-shaped with diagonals of 650–700 km*)—allows reaching most destinations within just 2 to 3 hours from centrally located Poznań or Warsaw, with even the most remote corners taking 4 hours at the absolute most.
* 400–450 miles
